title: Present Perfect Simple: All Uses, Stative Verbs & For/Since
grammarTitle: Present Perfect Simple — The Complete Guide
grammarNote: Present Perfect Simple (have/has + past participle) — одно из самых важных и часто используемых времён в английском. На B1 уровне вы должны уметь различать все его значения, правильно использовать FOR и SINCE, понимать стативные глаголы, и выбирать между PPS и Past Simple с уверенностью.

grammarTable.subject: Completed action + result
grammarTable.example: "She has finished the report." (It's done — the report exists.) ✅

grammarTable.subject: Life experience
grammarTable.example: "Have you ever been to Istanbul?" / "I've never tried durian." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Recent news/announcement
grammarTable.example: "She's just published a paper." / "They've recently moved." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Duration (FOR/SINCE)
grammarTable.example: "I've known her for ten years." / "She's been here since 2022." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Counting completions
grammarTable.example: "He's read 12 books this year." / "I've visited 8 countries." ✅

grammarTable.subject: With THIS week/year/ever
grammarTable.example: "She's written 3 essays this semester." (semester not over) ✅

grammarExtra.title: FOR vs SINCE: period of time vs starting point

rows.example: "I've known her FOR three years." / "FOR a long time." / "FOR ages." ✅
"I've known her SINCE 2021." / "SINCE Monday." / "SINCE I was a child." ✅

rows.form: FOR = how long / SINCE = when it started
rows.example: The key: FOR = duration (3 years). SINCE = starting point (2021). ✅
✅ "I've known her FOR three years." — three years = duration → FOR. ✅
✅ "I've known her SINCE 2021." — 2021 = starting point → SINCE. ✅

rows.form: How long have you...? → FOR answers
rows.example: "How long have you lived here?" → "For three years." / "Since 2021." ✅ (both work!)

grammarExtra.title: Stative verbs — PPS only, never PPC

rows.example: ✗ "I've been knowing her." → ✅ "I've KNOWN her for years." ✅
✗ "I've been liking this song." → ✅ "I've liked this song since I heard it." ✅
✗ "She's been owning that car for 5 years." → ✅ "She's OWNED it for 5 years." ✅
✗ "It's been seeming difficult." → ✅ "It's SEEMED difficult." ✅
✗ "I've been forgetting." (habit is ok) vs ✅ "I've FORGOTTEN." (completed) ✅
"I've lived here for 3 years." (stative-like) AND "I've been living here for 3 years." (both natural!) ✅

grammarExtra.title: PPS vs Past Simple — the critical distinction

rows.form: PPS = past action with PRESENT relevance
rows.example: "She has passed the exam." (result now: she has passed) ✅

rows.form: Past Simple = completed action, past focus
rows.example: "She passed the exam in June." (specific past time — done, no explicit present connection) ✅
"I saw him YESTERDAY." ✅ NOT "I have seen him yesterday." ✗ (yesterday = specific past time)
"I've lost my keys!" (result now: I can't get in) ✅
American: "Did you eat?" (asking recently). British: "Have you eaten?" ✅ Both correct in context.
"She hasn't finished YET." / "He's ALREADY left." / "She's JUST arrived." ✅
"Have you EVER been to Almaty?" / "I've NEVER tried this." ✅
"She's JUST finished." / "I've RECENTLY started." / "Things have changed LATELY." ✅
"I've ALREADY eaten." / "They haven't arrived YET." / "She STILL hasn't called." ✅

rows.form: for / since → PPS or PPC (with duration)
rows.example: "I've known her FOR years." (PPS stative) / "I've been studying FOR 3 hours." (PPC) ✅
"She's written 3 essays THIS semester." (semester open) ✅
"I saw him YESTERDAY/LAST WEEK/IN 2020." → Past Simple always ✅

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Most common PPS errors at B1

rows.example: ✅ "I saw him yesterday." — specific past time → Past Simple. ✅
✅ "I've KNOWN her for years." — "know" = stative. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "She has finished the report last year."
rows.example: ✅ "She finished the report last year." — specific past time. ✅
✅ "I've never BEEN to Paris." — past participle of "go" = "been" (for travel). ✅
✅ "How long HAVE YOU LIVED here?" — still living = PPS/PPC. ✅

grammarTip:
Present Perfect Simple — всё в одном:

has/have + PAST PARTICIPLE

1. Результат: "She has finished the report."
2. Опыт: "Have you ever been to Istanbul?"
3. Недавние события: "He's just arrived."
4. Длительность (стативные): "I've known her FOR 10 years."
5. Счёт: "She's published 3 papers this year."

FOR = продолжительность (for 3 years)
SINCE = начало (since 2021, since Monday)

Стативные глаголы → ТОЛЬКО PPS:
✗ I've been knowing → ✅ I've known
✗ I've been liking → ✅ I've liked

Конкретное прошедшее время → Past Simple!
✗ "I have seen him yesterday" 
✅ "I saw him yesterday"

Сигналы: ever/never/just/already/yet/recently

exercises.text: "She ___ (finish) the project. We can submit it now."
exercises.hint: Result = important NOW. "She HAS FINISHED the project." → result: now we can submit. ✅
"Have you ever TRIED horse milk?" — life experience → PPS + ever. ✅

exercises.text: "She has lived in Uralsk ___ three years."
exercises.hint: "three years" = duration → FOR. "FOR three years." ✅

exercises.text: "He has been studying English ___ he was twelve."
exercises.hint: "when he was twelve" = starting point → SINCE. "SINCE he was twelve." ✅

exercises.instruction: PPS vs Past Simple — specific time?
exercises.hint: "Last Tuesday" = specific past time → PAST SIMPLE. "I SAW that film last Tuesday." ✅
"know" = stative → PPS. "I'VE KNOWN her for ten years." ✅ Never "been knowing." ✅
Counting completions → PPS. "She HAS VISITED twelve countries." ✅
"just" + recent event = PPS. "He HAS JUST ARRIVED." ✅
Negative + "YET" = PPS for something expected but not done. "She hasn't submitted YET." ✅
"has ALREADY EATEN." — present result (not hungry now). ✅

exercises.instruction: PPS vs Past Simple — result now?
exercises.hint: "I HAVE LOST my keys!" — result matters NOW (I can't get in). PPS for current relevance. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ (write) three essays this semester." (semester not over)
exercises.hint: "This semester" = still open → PPS. "She HAS WRITTEN three essays this semester." ✅ (counting completions)
"I've never BEEN to a horse race." — for travel/visits: go → BEEN (not "gone"). "Have you BEEN to...?" ✅

opts: Wrong — "studied" should be "been studying" or "studied" is fine; "how long" often prefers PPC
exercises.correct: Wrong — "studied" should be "been studying" or "studied" is fine; "how long" often prefers PPC
exercises.hint: "How long HAVE YOU BEEN STUDYING here?" (PPC) is more natural. "Have you studied" = also possible but less natural for duration. ✅
"Have you HEARD from Rustam recently?" — PPS for recent, result-oriented question. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ (not / reply) yet. Should I send another message?"
exercises.hint: "She HASN'T REPLIED yet." — PPS negative + "yet." ✅
"In 1998" = specific past time → Past Simple. "The company OPENED its first branch in 1998." ✅

opts: "He's just called. He's on his way."
exercises.correct: "He's just called. He's on his way."
exercises.hint: "He's just called." — PPS + just = recent event with present relevance. ✅ All others have errors.

opts: Both haven't slept and haven't been sleeping work
exercises.correct: Both haven't slept and haven't been sleeping work
exercises.hint: "HAVEN'T SLEPT well lately" (PPS ✅) / "HAVEN'T BEEN SLEEPING well lately" (PPC ✅) — both natural for ongoing pattern. ✅
"want" is stative → "I'VE WANTED to visit Georgia." ✅ However, "wanting" in continuous is sometimes used informally. ✅

opts: Completed actions with present relevance, experiences, and counting
questions.correct: Completed actions with present relevance, experiences, and counting
questions.hint: PPS = result (I've finished), experience (I've been to X), counting (I've read 3 books). ✅
FOR + period (three years). SINCE + starting point (2021, Monday, I was young). ✅

questions.text: "I've been knowing her for years." — What is wrong?
opts: "knowing" is wrong — "know" is stative; should be "known"
questions.correct: "knowing" is wrong — "know" is stative; should be "known"
questions.hint: ✅ "I'VE KNOWN her for years." — stative verb → PPS only. ✅

questions.text: "I have seen him yesterday." — What is wrong?
opts: "Yesterday" = specific past time → Past Simple needed: "I saw him yesterday"
questions.correct: "Yesterday" = specific past time → Past Simple needed: "I saw him yesterday"
questions.hint: Specific past time = Past Simple. ✅ "I SAW him yesterday." ✅
"HAS JUST FINISHED" — PPS + just = recent completion with present result (relief). ✅

questions.text: "Have you ever been to Almaty?" — "ever" signals:
questions.hint: "ever" with PPS = asking about any time in your life experience. ✅

opts: Something expected but not done (negative + yet)
questions.correct: Something expected but not done (negative + yet)
questions.hint: Negative + YET = something expected but not yet happened. PPS. ✅

questions.text: "She's written 3 essays this semester." — PPS because:
opts: It counts completions within an open time period
questions.correct: It counts completions within an open time period
questions.hint: PPS for counting within still-open time period (semester not over). ✅

opts: For travel/visits: "gone" = still away; "been" = went and came back
questions.correct: For travel/visits: "gone" = still away; "been" = went and came back
questions.hint: "Have you BEEN to Paris?" (and returned). "He's GONE to Paris" = he is still there now. ✅

questions.text: "How long have you lived here?" — Can you also say "have you been living"?
opts: No — "live" is stative, must use PPS
Yes — "live" can use PPC for duration too
questions.correct: Yes — "live" can use PPC for duration too
questions.hint: "I've lived here" (PPS, stative-like) ✅ AND "I've been living here" (PPC, duration-focused) ✅ — both are natural! ✅

questions.text: Which requires Past Simple, not PPS?
questions.hint: "LAST SEPTEMBER" = specific past time → Past Simple. "I STARTED the course last September." ✅

questions.text: "She has lived here since 2020." — SINCE because:
questions.hint: SINCE + starting point in time. "She's lived here SINCE 2020." = 2020 is when it started. ✅
